views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Enter the October 10-11 high-level talks in Washington in a negotiating posture, seeking to lock in de-escalation — specifically the postponement of the threatened Oct 1 30% hike on $250B and the Dec 15 15% List 4B hike — while preserving Beijing's red lines on structural (subsidy/tech-transfer) reform and Huawei. Maintain the goodwill signals already on the table (tariff-exemption lists, farm-goods exclusions) but make no new unreciprocated commitments. Do not escalate; the economy cannot afford a broader confrontation, and talks are the one credible path to unwind the tariff overhang.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading is driven by clear, firm-level and economy-wide damage visible as of the decision date. The US has built a tariff wall around ~$500B of Chinese goods — List 3 raised to 25% on $250B (May 10), List 4A at 15% on ~$110-125B (Sept 1) — with 30% on $250B threatened for Oct 1 and 15% on ~$170B (List 4B, cell phones/laptops) for Dec 15. More corrosive, Huawei was placed on the entity list (May 16) and lost Google GMS and US chip supply (May 20), a direct assault on China's tech-self-sufficiency crown jewel. The macro toll is visible: August industrial output rose just 4.4% y/y, the lowest single-month figure since 2002, PPI turned negative (-0.3%) for the first time in three years, manufacturing PMI was below 50 (contraction), and Q2 growth slowed to 6.2%, the weakest in 27 years; US-bound exports fell 6.5% in July. Added to that, CNY broke 7.0 and Washington designated China a currency manipulator (Aug 5). This is squarely a 'High' threat for China on the party-relative scale, though not existential given reserves, stimulus, and non-US market diversification, hence +0.5. The action stance is negotiate (+0.15) rather than escalate because the damage is already material and escalating further would deepen domestic weakness while inviting a 30%/Dec 15 response, whereas both sides have already signaled de-escalation intent — the US delayed its Oct 1 hike and delisted 400+ items, and China issued exemption lists and farm exclusions ahead of the talks. Committing more (concede_purchases) is premature until Washington matches; the correct posture is to negotiate for tariff relief and delay without unilateral concession on structural issues or Huawei.
key_factors: ~$500B tariff wall: 25% List 3, 15% List 4A (Sept 1), threatened 30% (Oct 1) and 15% List 4B (Dec 15)
Huawei Entity List (May 16) + Google GMS/chip cutoff (May 20) — tech self-sufficiency under direct attack
CNY breached 7.0 and US named China a currency manipulator (Aug 5)
August industrial output +4.4% y/y (weakest since 2002), PPI -0.3% (first negative in 3 yrs), PMI <50, Q2 GDP 6.2% (weakest in 27 yrs)
13th-round high-level talks Oct 10-11; both sides signaling goodwill (US delayed Oct 1 hike, delisted 400+ items; China exemption lists + farm exclusions)

US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
Google suspends Huawei's access to Android/GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales.
CNY breaks 7; US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator.
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110-125B of Chinese imports).
China announces first tariff-exemption list for some US products.
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs.
